meta.title: Benchmarked, Rarely Field-Tested: Computer Vision for End-of-Life Product Data in Industrial Ecology
meta.subtitle: A taxonomy of CV applications, mapped to physical scale and information type
meta.source: van Lierde et al., "Benchmarked, Rarely Field-Tested: Computer Vision for End-of-Life Product Data in Industrial Ecology" (review article) [citation: forthcoming], Table S2 (per-task descriptors). Verdicts are the article's; do not alter without changing the article.

maturityLevels.gloss: Mature, well-benchmarked, deployable within a stated caveat.
Exists but needs tuning or verification, or degrades out of domain.
maturityLevels.handling: Human-in-the-loop verify every field; propagate elevated uncertainty; flag EoL-degraded capture.

maturityLevels.gloss: Works only inside the narrow object class it was built for; generalization fails across classes.
maturityLevels.handling: Treat as unavailable for arbitrary products; do not populate.

maturityLevels.gloss: No method benchmarked for this output on the products of interest; shown only in principle or in an adjacent domain, so field performance is unknown.
maturityLevels.handling: Do not populate an inventory field; retain as human-authored, redundancy-checked (k-of-n).

maturityLevels.gloss: No method maps to the cell, or the cell is derived from other cells rather than directly sensed.

product.name: End-of-life desk fan
product.note: Representative multi-component WEEE product chosen for the visualization. The taxonomy is product-general: its axes are physical scale and information type, and the evidence behind the verdicts spans washing machines, laptops, smartphones and vehicles. The paper's Table S3 and Figure S1 walk this same desk fan through three disassembly stages.

cells.methodFamily: OCR + database matching; retrieval / one-shot recognition
cells.maturityNote: Validated and deployed in-domain, but degrades materially under EoL capture: label read 95.7% repair -> 90.8% reuse -> 39.7% recycler intake. Two datasets from one research group (the EoL read-rate gradient and the collection-site pilot), not independent replication.
cells.failureMode: EoL label degradation (damaged, dirty, skewed, distant); database coverage; not autonomous (human-in-the-loop selection).
cells.example: Washing-machine label reading on phone and tablet cameras (Sterkens et al. 2023); waste-device model identification in an instrumented sorting cell, 90.3% top-1 over 1,958 models of undamaged devices (Koyanaka & Kobayashi 2024); six-camera take-back-facility retrieval of degraded appliances at waste-category (not model) level, 93.6% accuracy / 88.4% mAP@5 (top-five retrieval precision), instrumented rig (C. Zhou et al. 2025); e-waste sampling-center and distribution-center pilots, model number read from 51.5% and 69.5% of legible label images, 18% of sampled devices unlabeled (Sterkens & Peeters 2024).

cells.methodFamily: Monocular metric depth; feed-forward multi-view geometry; (generation-based 3D = documentation only)
cells.maturityNote: Geometry approximate, observed; depth maps benchmarked on general scenes; product dimensioning itself demonstrated, not benchmarked. Weight an approximate quantity, not a measurement (about one estimate in four off by more than a factor of two); generation-based 3D is not measurement.
cells.failureMode: Visible-surface only; residual scale sensitivity to capture metadata; weight compounds geometry x material error.
cells.example: Single-image mass estimation (Standley et al. 2017; Lee et al. 2026; Wang et al. 2026). Geometry evidence: monocular metric depth (Hu et al. 2024, Metric3D v2; Bochkovskii et al. 2025, Depth Pro; Yang et al. 2024, Depth Anything V2; R. Wang et al. 2025, MoGe-2); multi-view geometry (J. Wang et al. 2025, VGGT; Keetha et al. 2025, MapAnything); phone depth sensing (Luetzenburg et al. 2021; Hamilton-Fletcher et al. 2024).

cells.maturityNote: Structurally empty: structure is resolved at the component scale. Evidence mark –; carries no row in Table S2.

cells.task: Wear / damage; repair / reuse / recycle triage
cells.methodFamily: Supervised defect detection; zero-shot anomaly detection (WinCLIP / AnomalyCLIP); VLM description; triage = value/material sorting
cells.maturityNote: Single-class instrumented grading; nothing under contributor-grade capture. Peer-reviewed narrow-class validation has arrived: laptop covers graded A-E at 86.7% end-to-end on unseen models, and severity-graded smartphone screens, both researcher-operated and lighting-sensitive.
cells.hardware: Edge-feasible in principle; validated capability rig-bound
cells.failureMode: No validation under realistic capture (lighting sensitivity documented); single-class range; deployed triage remains value/material sorting.
cells.example: Instrumented laptop-cover A-E grading, 86.7% end-to-end (Wu et al. 2026); smartphone screen severity grading (Mohandas et al. 2025); kiosk device grading, narrow class under instrumented capture (Bowles et al. 2012; Li & Huang 2021). Exterior vehicle damage assessment (Hasan et al. 2025) stays the adjacent-domain anchor; industry grading vocabulary for phones and tablets, defect levels in millimeters (CTIA Certification 2019).

cells.maturityNote: Naming feasible; fine-grained part identity not reliable; out-of-domain weak (15.7 mAP multi-domain).
cells.failureMode: Missing/degraded markings; out-of-domain weakness of zero-shot recognition.
cells.example: Component-marking OCR, as at product scale (Sterkens et al. 2023); open-vocabulary naming (Liu et al. 2025, Grounding DINO); multi-domain zero-shot weakness, 15.7 mAP (Popov et al. 2025); battery-type classification from markings in battery-sorting-facility photographs, precision 0.98 and recall 0.67 for packs of 300 g or more (0.88 and 0.54 below), context only: a type group, not part identity, with no clean-capture arm (Sterkens et al. 2022).

cells.methodFamily: Monocular metric depth; feed-forward multi-view geometry
cells.failureMode: Occlusion within assembly aggravates visible-surface limit; scale sensitivity.
cells.example: Single-image / multi-view geometry (Hu et al. 2024, Metric3D v2; Wang et al. 2025, VGGT).

cells.task: Detection, segmentation, counting, attachment relations (Bill of Components)
cells.methodFamily: Closed-set / open-set detection; foundation segmentation + class-assignment; (image -> articulation for relations)
cells.maturityNote: Detect/segment Partial (~98.8% mAP50 on a narrow benchmark, needs domain tuning; segmentation trained at one waste-sorting facility falls from 56.0 to 45.5 mIoU at another). BoC relations Emerging-but-narrow (relations only for articulated household categories or toy vehicles; graph-topology accuracy also falls from ~82% to ~39% on an unseen dataset of the same kinds). The detect/segment sub-verdict rests on a single source: one lab-captured teardown benchmark.
cells.failureMode: Out-of-domain and zero-shot weakness (needs domain adaptation + class-assignment layer); no general attachment graph.
cells.example: E-waste / laptop teardown segmentation (Zhang et al. 2026); cross-facility waste segmentation (Bashkirova et al. 2023); class-assigning foundation segmentation (Carion et al. 2025, SAM 3); image -> articulation (Liu 2025 SINGAPO; Chen 2024 URDFormer; Yuan 2025 LARM).

cells.methodFamily: Supervised defect detection; connector-state (requirements level, per-unit only on lab-corroded screws); embodied/VLA (immature)
cells.maturityNote: Plausible-but-unvalidated; connector-state absent from products (requirements level, per-unit only on lab-corroded screws on test plates); centralized-cell-bound where demonstrated.
cells.hardware: Server- and cell-bound for demonstrated capability
cells.failureMode: No validated decentralized per-unit grading; embodied disassembly unreliable (0/20 unaided).
cells.example: Robotic disassembly cells (Liu et al. 2026, RAISE; Liu et al. 2025, VLA selective disassembly). Connector-state evidence: requirements level (Saenz et al. 2024); rust grading on lab-corroded screws on test plates (Mandolini et al. 2026); vision-guided screw removal that completed disassembly on 72 of 92 in-scope air-conditioner units (Ishikura et al. 2026); fastener/screw detection for cobot disassembly (Sutradhar et al. 2025).

cells.task: Surface and subsurface material ID (Bill of Materials)
cells.methodFamily: RGB classification (controlled); one/few-shot similarity (needs mask); few-shot VLM; dense surface segmentation
cells.maturityNote: Surface-region ID, controlled conditions only; no quantified composition of what a camera cannot see (interiors, coatings, alloys). The one image-based material-ID sorter precedent (a pilot-scale shredded-WEEE trial, Vogelgesang et al. 2025) characterizes a de-identified aggregate stream, not a per-unit intact product, so no per-unit deployed precedent exists (deployment gate ✗).
cells.rubricMarks: B · ✗ᵃ · ✗ (close-adjacent benchmark: in-the-wild material appearance, not EoL products)
cells.failureMode: Multi-material label compositeness (~90% TrashNet -> ~40% MultiWaste); domain shift (historical extreme: a legacy RGB pipeline fell from 100% to ~12–28% overall at the two hand-held illumination shifts, 0% on up to 3 of 4 classes; a third, robot-arm run at 77 lx kept ~78%); clutter in realistic scenes.
cells.example: Zero-shot VLM material recognition (Funk et al. 2026); controlled RGB material classification (Penumuru et al. 2020); 3D surface material segmentation (Li 2024 MaterialSeg3D; Drehwald 2023); circuit-board photographs to a component-level bill of masses, four off-the-shelf boards (Chedotel et al. 2026).

cells.methodFamily: Derived: component geometry x material class x density prior
cells.maturityNote: Absent as a standalone method; compounds geometry + identity uncertainty. Derived, so evidence mark –.
cells.failureMode: Compounds both inputs; image-to-mass methods tested only on off-the-shelf circuit boards, whole catalog objects, and discarded packaging and food items imaged by calibrated smart-bin cameras.

cells.maturityNote: Structurally empty: structure is resolved at the component scale. Evidence mark –; carries no row in Table S2.

cells.failureMode: Domain shift; clutter; no validated per-region condition grading.
cells.example: Surface segmentation (Li et al. 2024, MaterialSeg3D); particle segmentation for size monitoring of crushed aggregates, simulated images (Y. Zhou et al. 2025, ParticleSAM).
